cohort_answer.text: A) Rotateq (RV5): live attenuated pentavalent bovine-human reassortment vaccine (x3 doses), strains G1/G2/G3/G4 (human) x P7[5] (bovine), G6 (bovine) x P1[8] (human). Rotarix (RV1): live attenuated monovalent vaccine from single human strain RIX44144 (x2 doses). B) Rotateq - human-bovine reassortment (5); Rotarix - human strain only (1). C) Rotateq: 3 doses, routine, start at 6 weeks; Rotarix: 2 doses, min 4 weeks apart, start at 6 weeks; both must give last dose before 8 months. D) Serious allergy to vaccine component or previous dose; history of intussusception or greater susceptibility; known immunodeficiency (SCID); >8 months of age. Precautions: altered immunocompetence, moderate-severe illness including acute gastroenteritis, chronic GI disease. E) Rotateq: 3 oral doses at 2,4,6 months (first dose 6-12 weeks, last before 8 months, min q4 weeks); Rotarix: 2 oral doses. F) Generally well tolerated; small increased risk of intussusception, hematochezia; incidence of fever, vomiting, diarrhea ≥1% higher in vaccinees vs controls after each dose.

parts.text: A. Pathogenesis of diarrhea in rotavirus

cohort_answer.text:
A: Poorly understood. Malabsorption from mucosal damage and suppression of brush border enzymes. Enterotoxin leads to secretory state. Villi blunted and shorter

B: Hx of intussusception. Known immunodeficiency (SCID). Known hypersensitivity. Severe anaphylactic allergy
